description:
About Factory

Our mission is to create a world where software builds and improves itself.

We build the platform for self-improving software development, helping the world's largest enterprise engineering teams turn their organizations into autonomous software factories. Customers including Nvidia, Blackstone, Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), Palo Alto Networks, Adobe, and T-Mobile run Factory to ship code, review PRs, run tests, and deploy continuously - getting smarter with every cycle.

In 2026, we raised $200M at a $5B valuation, bringing our total funding to over $400M. We are backed by world-class investors and operators including Khosla Ventures, Sequoia, Blackstone, Ali Ghodsi (CEO of Databricks), and Frank Slootman (Former CEO of Snowflake).

About the Role

Factory is hiring a Regional Director to build the Enterprise Solutions Engineering team. Our Enterprise Solutions Engineers own the full customer lifecycle, pre-sales and post-sales: discovery, demos, proofs of concept, security and architecture reviews, pilot delivery, and the ongoing adoption and expansion of Factory once a customer is live. You will help build out the team, define how it runs, and own both the technical win and the production outcome for our Enterprise accounts with the fastest growth.

You will hire and coach the people who do this work, set the standard for how it is done, and stay close enough to the accounts to do it yourself when it matters. You will work directly with Enterprise Sales leadership, and closely with Product and Engineering. This is a hands-on leadership role that builds the team from the start and links Sales, Product, and Engineering. It suits someone who combines real technical fluency, strong people leadership, and sound judgment under deal pressure.

What You Will Do and Achieve

  • Build the Enterprise Solutions Engineering team: define the hiring profile, recruit and close the founding Solutions Engineers, and grow the team with the Enterprise pipeline

  • Design and iterate the team's operating playbook across the full lifecycle: discovery, pilot scoping, success metrics, security and compliance reviews, production rollout, and ongoing adoption and expansion

  • Own the team's technical win rate, time-to-technical-win, pilot-to-production conversion, and post-sales adoption and expansion; report them to GTM leadership and use them to coach the team

  • Work with Account Executives and Sales leadership so that each discovery call, demo, and proof of concept is high quality and tied to a customer outcome

  • Carry accounts directly while the team ramps, and take over when an evaluation gets complex, a deployment is at risk, or a large Enterprise deal needs senior help, including with CTO, VP Engineering, and Security stakeholders

  • Onboard, coach, and develop Solutions Engineers; give each SE clear expectations, a career path, and performance standards, and shorten ramp time with structured enablement

  • Turn what customers and prospects tell the team into clear, actionable feedback for Product and Engineering

Qualifications

You do not need to meet every requirement to be a strong candidate. If this role excites you and you have related experience, we encourage you to apply.

  • 4+ years leading Enterprise Solutions Engineering, Field Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or customer engineering teams at an enterprise software company, spanning pre-sales and post-sales, including at least one team you built or scaled from a small starting point

  • A strong hiring track record: you know how to source, assess, and close senior technical customer-facing talent

  • A strong technical foundation and fluency in modern software development workflows, developer tooling, CI/CD, and AI coding tools

  • You partner well with Sales and still keep every technical answer honest, so customers keep trusting us

  • Calm under customer pressure: you can take over a stalled evaluation or a struggling deployment and move it forward

  • Operational discipline: you track technical win rates and pilot outcomes and run a team on the numbers, not on anecdotes

  • Executive presence, and clear communication with every audience, from the developers on a pilot to the CTO who signs off

  • A builder and player-coach mindset: you do your best work in a fast-moving startup, and you add structure where the team has none yet

Nice to Have

  • Hands-on experience with agentic coding tools, LLM-based products, or developer platform sales

  • Background as a software engineer or in a technical consulting role

  • Experience standing up a new team or function for a high-growth company
